display.title: Hashavas Aveidah: The Rebbe Rashab's Chassid and the Lost Wallet, Part 2
display.summary_short: For Chof-Beis Shevat, Rebbetzin Chaya Mushka's sensitivity to others; then the Rebbe Rashab promises a Chassid ten times the reward he refused, and the blessing comes true.
display.summary_long: In the week of Chof-Beis Shevat, the yahrzeit of Rebbetzin Chaya Mushka, the storyteller explains the Rebbe's words that the living should take it to heart: this world is like a marketplace, and only here, with a body, can we do mitzvos. He shares a story heard from a friend about how the Rebbetzin served a shy young guest ice cream herself, so he would get enough, and teaches the children to be sensitive to other people's feelings. Then the story continues from last week. Yeshua Binyamin tells the Rebbe Rashab of his troubles and, when asked, about the wallet he returned. The Rebbe Rashab says that because he refused payment for the mitzvah, Hashem will give him ten times as much, hands him a coin for blessing, and tells him to accept if he is offered a job as a chazzan. Leaders of a nearby community soon ask him to lead the davening for Rosh Hashanah and Yom Kippur. On the way home he visits a dying old wagon driver who mistakes him for his servant and reveals a wallet he once stole and hid under a rock. Inside are exactly three thousand rubles, with no way to find the owner.
display.lesson: Be sensitive to other people's feelings, and a mitzvah done without wanting a reward brings Hashem's blessing many times over.
